blocks.text: “Three generations of actors from The Hunger Games are here with us. Everybody came. I’ve loved working with all of you. Thank you so much for sharing your talents with us for these stories,” he said in remarks before the film unspooled Monday night at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall in New York.
Lionsgate is releasing it in theaters this weekend.

“So, what I’m going to do is I’m just going to call out some of our cast, and just please stand up when I call your name. It’s too many people to bring out on stage. But we have Ray Fiennes here today. Glenn Close is here tonight. We have Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Billy Porter, Percy Daggs, Molly McCann.”

Kieran Culkin, Lili Taylor, Maya Hawke, Ben Wang and Scott Greenan there. So were Iona Bell, Rada Ray, Jefferson White, Jhaleil Swaby, Kaine Buffonge, Kelvin Harrison Jr. and Edvin Ryding, with Brad Simpson and Iris Apatow, Andrés Rivera, Willow Shields, Tom Blyth and more.
“And then, of course, we have Whitney Peak. And we have Joe Zada,” he said of the star-crossed Lenore Dove and Haymitch Abernathy.

“But the special thing is that tonight we also have Tom Blythe, Rachel Zegler, and going way back to the very beginning, Elizabeth Banks, Jena Malone, Amandla Stenberg. Willow Shields. And then, because certain actors let the cat out of the bag, I will say that Woody [Harrelson] is here tonight. Josh Hutcherson (Peta) and Jennifer Lawrence (Katniss) are here.”

The director, accompanied on stage by producer Nina Jacobson, wholeheartedly thanked writer Suzanne Collins, on on whose books the films are based. “Without Suzanne, none of us would be here. I mean, 14 years of my life,” he said. “Your themes, the ideas that you want to write about, the worlds that you build, the narratives that you weave are just unbelievable.”
Sunrise on the Reaping is the fifth book and sixth film in the series. ( Hunger Games: Mockingjay was split in two parts.) Lawrence directed all but the first.

Set 24 years before Katniss Everdeen’s story, the plot of the latest installment begins on the morning of the reaping for the 50th annual Hunger Games (the Second Quarter Quell), where twice as many tributes (48 children) are reaped, including 16-year-old Haymitch from District 12.

Adam Fogelson , chair of Lionsgate’s Motion Pictures Group, recalled an invitation several years ago from Collins and [her literary agent] Jason Dravis “to sit on a couch in a yard in Los Angeles and read a manuscript of Sunrise on the Reaping . And it will be one of the great days of my professional life.”

In part, he said in opening remarks, “because I had the privilege of reading another of her extraordinary works long before anyone in the general public would. And, if I’m being candid, more selfishly, because I could imagine how spectacular a film we were probably going to end up with a few years later.

“And now, to be here with all of you today, with you about to witness what’s been created, is a great joy for me. I knew it was likely to be great because of the extraordinary creative team that we knew we were going to have working on this project. I couldn’t imagine that beyond incredible screenwriters, incredible producers, and incredible directors, we would also assemble one of the most extraordinary casts ever put together for a motion picture.”
